name: Video Frequency Spectrum
description: Analyzes frequency spectrum of video frames
algorithm: Video Frequency Spectrum — Frequency Domain Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes the video frequency spectrum for forensic detection:

1. **2D Spatial Frequency Analysis**: Per-frame 2D FFT reveals the spatial frequency spectrum. The method analyzes the overall spectral shape, spectral peaks, and spectral symmetry. Natural images follow approximately 1/f spectral decay.

2. **Spectral Anomaly Detection**: AI generators produce characteristic spectral anomalies: (a) GAN checkerboard peaks at upsampling stride frequencies, (b) diffusion model spectral gaps at certain frequency bands, (c) autoencoder spectral truncation at the bottleneck resolution. The method detects these architecture-specific spectral signatures.

3. **Face-Background Spectral Comparison**: The spatial frequency spectrum of face regions and background should be consistent (same imaging pipeline). The method compares spectral shapes — generated faces may show different spectral characteristics (different noise spectrum, different high-frequency falloff, or additional spectral peaks from generation artifacts).

4. **Temporal Spectral Stability**: The spatial frequency spectrum should be temporally stable for static content. The method tracks spectral stability — deepfake generation may produce temporally varying spectral content as the generator's output fluctuates frame-to-frame.

5. **3D Spatio-Temporal Spectrum**: The combined spatial-temporal frequency spectrum (3D FFT over x, y, t) reveals motion structure. Natural motion produces characteristic spatio-temporal spectral planes. AI-generated motion may show different spectral structure — particularly at the temporal frequency boundaries of the generation model.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through video frequency spectrum analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Verdoliva, L. (2020). Media Forensics and DeepFakes: An Overview. IEEE JSTSP.
Zheng, Y. et al. (2021). Exploring Temporal Coherence for More General Video Face Forgery Detection. ICCV.
